meta.name: ja_lints_research
meta.purpose: Seed lexicons for Haruka's Japanese prompt-quality lint rules: vague/hands-off wording, politeness padding, clear task statements, and output-shape specifications.
meta.method: Every entry was collected from live Japanese-language web sources found via Japanese-language queries and actually fetched. No entry is a translation of an English wordlist. Where sources disagree on whether an expression belongs in a list, the disagreement is recorded on the entry rather than silently resolved.
caveats: confidence is a research artifact, not a tuned weight. 'high' = multiple independent Japanese sources name the expression AND explain why it fails; 'medium' = attested as vague/padding but studied in a different frame (e.g. conversational hedging rather than instructions); 'low' = seed word we could not corroborate from any Japanese source that treats it as problematic.

The three 'low' vague entries (サクッと / ちゃちゃっと / まるっと) came from the original seed brief. Japanese dictionaries define them neutrally. They are retained with disagreement notes so the decision to include or drop them is explicit, not accidental.
パパッと was in the seed brief but could not be sourced at all and is deliberately absent.

The canonical Japanese style guides do NOT contain vague-vocabulary lists. JTF日本語標準スタイルガイド was checked and covers orthography and punctuation only. Japanese vagueness lists live in software-requirements writing, management/coaching blogs, and design-brief blogs instead. Do not cite JTF as authority for the vague_words rule.

Length markers (〜文字以内で etc.) are detectable but multiple Japanese verification articles report that LLMs frequently fail to obey them. Detecting the marker is not the same as the constraint being honored.

verification.method: Independent agent re-fetched 10 load-bearing content URLs and 8 license claims and was instructed to look for failures rather than confirmations.
corrections_applied: doc.dev1x category names are question-form headings, not the labels previously quoted.
JTF style guide re-verified at 第4.0版 (2026-07-25); the no-vagueness-section negative result holds.
Three license errors found and corrected in the D2 report (JTF version history, UniDic licensing, NEologd status) — see LEXICON_REPORT.md.
unverified: Long-tail entries sourced from a single blog were not individually re-fetched; the 'low' confidence tier and per-entry disagreement notes mark where support is thin.
GitHub commit metadata was unreachable (API 403, /commits/ robots-blocked), so repo maintenance status rests on committed files and release pages.

vague_words.label_ja: あいまい・丸投げ表現
vague_words.description: Expressions people actually write in requests and prompts that leave the work under-specified or hand the judgment to the other party.

productive_patterns.pattern: [任意の主観的形容詞・オノマトペ] + 感じ|具合 + で|に
productive_patterns.why: The highest-yield finding across the design-brief sources. Japanese vague requests overwhelmingly form as [subjective adjective or onomatopoeia] + 感じ/具合 + で/に, which generates infinitely many surface forms (ラグジュアリーな感じで, イケてる感じで, シュッとした感じで, ぼわっと…). No static wordlist catches these.

productive_patterns.pattern: 指示語 with no antecedent in the prompt
productive_patterns.regex_sketch: (?:あの|例の|その|この)(?:件|やつ|アレ|あたり|辺)
productive_patterns.why: こそあど reference to context the reader does not have. Distinct failure mode from vague adverbs.

suggested_fix_templates.note: Three Japanese sources independently converge on the same repair, which gives the lint three distinct suggestion shapes rather than one generic scold.

entries.note: Conditional. Forbes says it is legitimate for 概算・概要 at an early stage but casual and unfit for formal docs, and warns 相手が期待する詳細度を確認する必要がある. Acceptable when a tolerance follows.

cushion_words.description: Politeness padding at the head of a request. Detected so it can be discounted when measuring prompt specificity.

action_key.strip: True zero-information padding. Safe to discount entirely when scoring specificity.
action_key.flag: Encodes a real constraint (grants an out, waives urgency). Discounting it silently upgrades a soft ask to a hard one.
action_key.keep: Not padding at all — asserts a fact. Removing it deletes information.

matching_notes: Cushions STACK, and the Japanese sources treat stacking as the defect rather than any individual phrase. Oggi prescribes 1文に1つのクッション言葉. A prompt head can carry three in a row (お忙しいところ + 大変恐縮ではございますが + お手数をおかけしますが). Match greedily and repeatedly from position 0, not once.
Trailing connective is highly variable and must be optional: が / ですが / ではございますが / のですが / なのですが / ますが / けれど — and several forms appear bare with no が at all (あいにく, 残念ながら, 僭越ながら, おかげさまで, 念のため).
Intensifier prefix is a free slot: 大変 / たいへん / 誠に / まことに / 重ね重ね / たびたび / もし / もしも.
Orthography genuinely varies in published business copy: お手隙／お手すき, ご面倒をおかけ／ご面倒をお掛け, 僭越ながら／せんえつながら, よろしければ／宜しければ, ご多忙／御多忙, 申し上げにくい／申しあげにくい, お伺い／おうかがい, 添えず／沿えず. Normalize first.
Pure-hiragana renderings of the noun (e.g. おてすう) did NOT appear in any source consulted. Do not assume they occur.
Several phrases the guides file as クッション言葉 are full clauses, not adverbials (お尋ねしてもよろしいでしょうか, お伺いしたいことがあるのですが). A pattern keyed only on 〜が heads will miss them.

task_verbs.description: Expressions that state a clear ask — the prompt actually names an action. Presence of one of these is positive signal for the instruction-clarity subscore.
matching_notes: The ください／下さい split is the single biggest practical issue. JTF日本語標準スタイルガイド mandates hiragana ください for the auxiliary verb, but the OFFICIAL prompt examples published by 東京都 and 千葉県 use 「要約して下さい」「表に整理して下さい」 in kanji. The linter must match both.
「〜こと」体言止め (解説をつけること) is a Japanese-specific instruction form used in constraint sections. English prompt-engineering lists have no counterpart, so nothing imported would cover it.

Match on POS, not raw string, where possible: 要約 as a bare noun in running text should not fire; 要約する／要約して in predicate position should. See textlint-rule-morpheme-match in the D2 report for MIT-licensed tooling that does this.

cross_list_notes: INTENTIONAL OVERLAPS — three families appear in two lists on purpose. (1) 対応する／検討する／最適化する are grammatically clear asks (task_verbs) but semantically empty ones (vague_words): a prompt reading only 対応してください should score as HAVING a task verb AND as vague. (2) わかりやすく／詳しく are weak output-shape specs (format_markers) that name a direction but no target (vague_words). Decide the scoring interaction deliberately; do not let both rules fire visibly on the same span.

The 適切に loop is worth a rubric note. Japanese politeness guides recommend 適切な as the formal upgrade for ざっくり／適当な, while prompt guides list 適切に as an NG prompt word. A de-vaguing rewrite can therefore produce text that trips the same rule. Never suggest 適切に as a fix.
Cushion detection should run BEFORE task-verb and format-marker detection. Cushions stack at position 0 and several contain verbs (お伺いしたいことがあるのですが) that would otherwise register as task verbs.

Orthographic normalization is load-bearing for all four lists. SudachiDict's normalized forms (正規化表記) and its synonym dictionary's 表記ゆれ column — both Apache 2.0 — solve this without license entanglement. See the D2 report.
